title: Carrying Capacity and Population Growth
seo_title: Grade 10 Science: Carrying Capacity and Population Growth Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_text: Population size and density; exponential and logistic growth; carrying capacity and limiting factors; interactions between species; human population and sustainability. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 10, Quarter 4: Life Science)
meta_desc: Free Grade 10 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 4: Life Science): population size and density, population growth, carrying capacity and limiting factors, interactions between species and human population and sustainability. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Logistic growth levels off at the carrying capacity.
body_html:
How to think about it

Population density = number of individuals ÷ area. The mark–recapture estimate is N = (number marked × number caught the second time) ÷ number recaptured with marks. A population grows when births and immigration are greater than deaths and emigration.

With unlimited resources, a population grows exponentially (a J-shaped curve). Limiting factors such as food, space and disease slow growth, giving a logistic, S-shaped curve that levels off at the carrying capacity. Density-dependent factors (competition, disease) get stronger as the population grows.

Example

50 Philippine deer are tagged. Later 40 are caught and 10 have tags. Estimate the population.

N = 50 × 40 ÷ 10

Answer: 200 Philippine deer

Example

A town of 2000 has 60 births, 20 deaths, 10 immigrants and 30 emigrants in a year. Change?

(60 + 10) − (20 + 30)

Answer: +20

Common mistakes

  • Thinking carrying capacity never changes: it changes when the environment does.
  • Calling a predator–prey relationship mutualism.
  • Forgetting immigration and emigration in population change.

faq.a: More prey feeds more predators; more predators then reduce the prey, so the predators fall too.
